subject: physics
question_text: A parachutist flying in an aeroplane jumps when it is at a height of 3 km above the ground. He opens his parachute when he is about 1 km above the ground. Describe his motion.

verification.note: Unit 3 has NO Long Answer section in either source book, so no 8-mark form is invented. The Fastrack (pp.6-8) lists 4 Very Short Answer and 6 Short Answer questions plus a PROBLEMS section; the TSBIE Basic Learning Material (pp.4-5) has a Short Answer section ONLY (5 questions) and no VSAQ section. The mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Motion in a Straight Line · 4 marks

steps.label: Before opening
lines: From 3 km to 1 km he falls freely.
His initial vertical velocity is zero, and he
keeps the horizontal velocity of the aeroplane.
He accelerates downward at g, so his
steps.why: He leaves a horizontally moving aeroplane, so his motion begins as a projectile: steady horizontal velocity with a vertical velocity that grows from zero.
common_mistakes: Saying he starts with a downward velocity. He starts with zero vertical velocity.
Forgetting the horizontal velocity carried from the aeroplane.

recall.must_convey: That from 3 km to 1 km he falls freely, starting with zero vertical velocity and accelerating downward at g while keeping the aeroplane’s horizontal velocity.

steps.memory_tip: Before the parachute: free fall at g, plus the plane’s horizontal velocity.
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Give both the vertical and horizontal parts.

steps.label: After opening
lines: At 1 km the parachute opens. Air resistance
and buoyancy now act upward, opposing his
weight, so the net downward force falls
steps.why: The parachute increases the surface area enormously, so the upward drag becomes large enough to exceed his weight for a while and slow him down.
common_mistakes: Saying he stops instantly when the parachute opens. He decelerates over a distance.

recall.must_convey: That when the parachute opens air resistance acts upward, the net force falls and he decelerates.

steps.memory_tip: The parachute adds AREA, so drag jumps and he slows.
steps.margin_note: Name the upward force: air resistance.

steps.label: Terminal velocity

lines.text: Drag soon balances weight, so a = 0

lines: From then he falls with a constant terminal
velocity in a straight line until he reaches
steps.why: Drag grows with speed, so as he slows the drag falls until it exactly matches his weight. At that point the acceleration is zero and the speed stops changing.
common_mistakes: Saying he keeps decelerating all the way to the ground. He settles at a constant terminal velocity.

recall.must_convey: That the drag soon balances his weight, the acceleration becomes zero and he falls at a constant terminal velocity.

steps.memory_tip: Drag rises with speed until it equals weight. Then a = 0 — terminal velocity.
steps.margin_note: The phrase "terminal velocity" is the mark.

insider_note: Both books ask this. Split the answer at the moment the parachute opens — before and after are two different motions.
